<a id="GnuPositions"></a>

### Positions in a file

`GnuPositions` · `src/text.ts:43`

How a message designates a place in a file: "file:line", the first line having the number 1.

Source: GNU Coding Standards, § 4.4 Formatting Error Messages · `https://www.gnu.org/prep/standards/html_node/Errors.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `firstLine` | `1` | The number of the first line of a file |
| `firstColumn` | `1` | The number of the first column of a line |
| `separator` | `:` | Separates the file from the line number |

<a id="InvisibleCharacters"></a>

### Characters that do not show

`InvisibleCharacters` · `src/text.ts:28`

The control characters (U+0000 to U+001F), the no-break space (U+00A0) and the line and paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029): written as they are, a reader cannot see them. JSON escapes the control characters, and leaves the others as they are.

Source: The Unicode Standard 15.1, § 23.1 Control Codes, § 6.2 General Punctuation (U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029); RFC 8259 § 7 · `https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode15.1.0/`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `hidden` | `[\u0000-\u001f\u00a0\u2028\u2029]` | Every character a reader cannot see, as a class of a regular expression |
| `leftByJson` | `[\u00a0\u2028\u2029]` | Those of them that JSON writes as they are |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [A published value is cited, not copied](product.md#CitedNotCopied)

<a id="TextFile"></a>

### Text file

`TextFile` · `src/text.ts:12`

What a line of a text file is: characters, then a newline, the last line included.

Source: POSIX.1-2017, Base Definitions, § 3.206 Line and § 3.403 Text File · `https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap03.html#tag_03_206`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `endOfLine` | `"\n"` | Ends each line, the last one included |

- Maintained by: trame

<a id="UnifiedDiff"></a>

### Unified differences

`UnifiedDiff` · `src/text.ts:60`

How two files or two trees differ, as GNU diff writes it: a header per pair of files, the lines removed and added, the files that only one tree holds.

Source: GNU diffutils: Comparing and Merging Files, § 2.2.3 Unified Format and § 4 Comparing Directories; POSIX.1-2017, diff · `https://www.gnu.org/software/diffutils/manual/html_node/Unified-Format.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `program` | `diff` | The program that compares |
| `options` | `-ru` | Recursively, in the unified format |
| `same` | `0` | The exit status when nothing differs |
| `differ` | `1` | The exit status when something differs |
| `header` | `"diff "` | Opens the differences of a pair of files |
| `onlyIn` | `"Only in "` | A file that only one tree holds |
| `oldFile` | `---` | Names the first file of a pair |
| `newFile` | `+++` | Names the second file of a pair |
| `removed` | `-` | Begins a line of the first file that the second does not have |
| `added` | `+` | Begins a line of the second file that the first does not have |
| `hunk` | `@@` | Opens and closes the ranges of a hunk: the lines of each file it covers |
| `rangeSeparator` | `,` | Separates the first line of a range from the number of its lines |
